answer: Slashable bonds resist sybils: to act, an identity locks collateral in a vault, and provable misbehavior forfeits it — honest work risks nothing, cheating loses the stake. The fable that one actor spawns a free orchard of accounts collapses when each fake must fund its own bond, and one caught clone loses the whole deposit. A swarm now wagers real capital per head, so mass fakery becomes a losing trade.
